title: Phonological Awareness
objective: Introduce the purpose, structure, and key skills developed in Phase 1.

learning_objectives: Recognize why it matters for reading
Become familiar with the five sections in Phase 1

payload.headline: What is Phonological Awareness

sentences.text: Phonological awareness is the ability to hear and work with sounds in spoken language.
Children who develop strong sound awareness learn to read and spell more easily.

payload.teacher_prompt: Explain that Phase 1 builds listening and sound skills.

payload.headline: Why It Matters

sentences.text: Before children learn letters, they must learn to hear parts of spoken language.
This includes rhyming, counting words, clapping syllables, and hearing beginning and ending sounds.

payload.teacher_prompt: Give simple examples from real objects.

payload.headline: What Your Child Will Learn

sentences.text: Phase 1 has playful activities that build listening and sound skills.
Children learn to hear rhymes, count words, break words into syllables, and notice individual sounds.

payload.teacher_prompt: Introduce this before Unit 1 so learners know the plan.

payload.headline: The Five Sections in Phase 1

sentences.text: Learning Sensorially builds early listening through hands on activities.
Rhyming teaches children to match words that sound alike.
Words and Sentences helps children count and organize words.
Syllables teaches children to clap, break, and blend word parts.
Phonemic Awareness helps children work with individual sounds.

payload.teacher_prompt: Explain what each section focuses on and how they connect.

home_practice: Play rhyming games like cat, hat, and bat.
Notice beginning sounds in objects around the home.

summary_hint: An introduction to Phase 1 covering the purpose and the five key skill areas.
